semantic_judging.note: Full re-judge of the entire translation (177 elements, 3 judges) with ground-truth-enriched judging (see ontology_translation/TODO.md 2026-08-17 log): judges now see the real, independently-resolved source class definitions for the classes each element involves, not just the compiler's own self-reported evidence text. Found and fixed two real bugs in the grounding resolution itself before trusting the results: (1) PascalCase/camelCase class-name normalization -- compiled names like CondensingUnit never matched space-separated source labels like "Condensing Unit", silently dropping ground truth for almost every multi-word class; (2) judge-prompt calibration -- an action's ground truth only ever covers its input class, and the prompt wording let judges over-read that partial coverage as evidence against the action. The corrected run found 6 genuinely unsupported and 15 contested elements, converging on one real pattern: every status property in the file used an identical templated justification ("rec datatype property status; standard <X> operating state practice"), which held up under real per-class scrutiny for equipment (AHU, Fan, Chiller...) but not consistently for sensors/valves. Ran the 9 affected items (plus the CO2 ventilation rule) through repair.py: 3 valve properties renamed status -> position (the allowed values were fine, the property name was the unsupported part), 3 items regrounded with stronger specific evidence (majority was already supported, just contested), 3 sensor status properties genuinely dropped (no defensible grounding and no honest narrower replacement). All resulting elements independently re-judged afterward: unanimous supported, 0 unsupported, 0 contested. Total real Azure cost across this whole re-judge/repair/verify lineage: $1.6381.
